facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old African American female
elevated intraocular pressure at age 13
taller stature than her relatives (180.4 cm)
long fingers
hypermobility of the shoulders, digits, and knees
Family history was negative for similar findings
Serial echocardiograms showed no abnormalities
Open iridocorneal angle in each eye
No evidence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion
Subtle lens dislocation superonasally in the right eye (first observed at age 17)
Later developed lens dislocation in the left eye (at age 32)
2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene (c.709C>T p.Arg237* and c.3776-1G>C splice acceptor)

concepts.why: The patient has elevated intraocular pressure and open iridocorneal angle, which are consistent with Pseudoexfoliation Syndrome
The patient has tall stature, long fingers, and hypermobility, which are characteristic of Marfan Syndrome, and also has lens dislocation, which is a common feature of the disease
The patient has hypermobility, which is a key feature of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome
The patient has elevated intraocular pressure and no evidence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion, which are consistent with Primary Congenital Glaucoma
The presence of lens dislocation and elevated intraocular pressure, combined with the genetic finding of heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene, points towards Weill-Marchesani Syndrome.

rationales.F04: Long fingers are a characteristic feature of Weill-Marchesani Syndrome and Marfan Syndrome.
rationales.F05: Hypermobility is a key feature of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome.
rationales.F08: Open iridocorneal angle rules out Primary Congenital Glaucoma.
rationales.F09: Absence of Haab striae, buphthalmos, or high iris insertion rules out Primary Congenital Glaucoma.
rationales.F10: Lens dislocation is a characteristic feature of Weill-Marchesani Syndrome and Marfan Syndrome.
rationales.F11: Bilateral lens dislocation increases the likelihood of Weill-Marchesani Syndrome.
rationales.F12: The presence of LTBP2 gene variants is not typical of the listed conditions, making them less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of 2 heterozygous variants in the LTBP2 gene and the combination of lens dislocation, tall stature, and joint hypermobility point towards Weill-Marchesani Syndrome, which is further supported by the absence of significant cardiac abnormalities that would be expected in Marfan Syndrome.
